battery_utility_scale.why: ERAA utility-scale batteries in the market

battery_utility_scale_out_of_market.why: TSO-owned reserve asset, outside the day-ahead market (R-STO-8)

biogas.why: biogas engines run as other renewable

biomass.why: biomass in the Baltic fleets is CHP

capacity_mechanism.why: S1's future capacity mechanism, entered 'simply as gas plants' (D-036)

coal_gas.why: ENTSO-E's coal-derived gas in Estonia is oil-shale retort gas (R-SUP-4)

controllable_need.why: Elering's need for controllable capacity, not a fleet (shown as a note)

gas.why: the owner's generic gas fleet bids as a present CCGT

gas_existing.why: S1's existing natural gas names no technology; with the rest of S1's gas as peaking (D-036)

gas_ocgt.why: Elering's gas tender: fast peaking units

gas_reserve_procurement.why: S1's reserve procurement: fast gas units (D-036)

gas_restoration.why: S1's distributed restoration tender, entered 'simply as gas plants' (D-036)

hydro_small.why: small hydro runs on its inflow

kiisa.why: Kiisa emergency reserve plant: TSO-owned reserve asset, outside the day-ahead market (R-STO-8)

natural_gas.why: ERAA's aggregate natural-gas capacity bids as a present CCGT

oil.why: ENTSO-E A68 lists 8 MW (2020) and 52 MW (2022) of oil in Estonia and no output of it (D-013)

oil_shale.why: R-SUP-4: Auvere, then fluidised bed, then pulverised firing

oil_shale_new.why: PEMMDB's new oil shale is the fluidised-bed technology: Auvere, then Balti 11 and Eesti 8

oil_shale_old.why: PEMMDB's old oil shale is pulverised firing

pondage.why: PEMMDB/ERAA pondage: in Latvia, the Daugava cascade

solar_pv_rooftop_industrial.why: ERAA rooftop PV (behind the meter, R-DEM-2)

solar_pv_rooftop_residential.why: ERAA rooftop PV (behind the meter, R-DEM-2)

solar_thermal_without_storage.why: ERAA solar thermal without storage produces on the solar profile

thermal.why: Litgrid's aggregate thermal capacity names no technology; the Lithuanian presets take their thermal classes from ERAA (shown as a note)

hydro_inflow_twh.ror.note: TYNDP 2024's inflow as published; the engine takes it as given output

hydro_inflow_twh.daugava.note: TYNDP 2024's inflow as published; the engine takes the Daugava's at the record's level, times the factor of D-070

EE.method: bisection on the cycling cost until the engine of record's Estonian batteries discharge what A75 reports from the week of its first report; per mFRR share
EE.why: OPEN-3 decided by the owner (D-025): the batteries hold no mFRR, and their cycling cost is the fit at that share; it applies to every zone's batteries

biomass.method: average hourly A75 generation, per 1 °C bin (bins of ≥ 50 h), of the fit years' hours whose observed zone price was below the technology's cheapest bid in the engine (before the floor and the markup); least-squares line on the bins' average heating degree-hours weighted by their hours, a, b ≥ 0; T_ref of {8, 10, 12, 15} °C with the least squared error

gas_bid.method: one bid for every gas offer of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, a combined-cycle plant's cost (gas_ccgt) plus one adder: the average of the adders each fit year gives alone on a grid of 10 EUR/MWh from 0 to 150 and of 2.5 EUR/MWh around its best, objective sum of the three zones' hourly price MAE of that year; engine of record; at Kruonis's step 60 EUR/MWh, the step of the grid whose register fits the two years best (D-115, D-164; the grid: step 0: 45, 64.56; step 15: 43.75, 62.97; step 30: 42.5, 62; step 45: 42.5, 61.51; step 60: 42.5, 61.43; step 90: 42.5, 61.59); 2023 alone 42.5 (26.89 on it, 34.54 on the other); 2024 alone 42.5 (34.54 on it, 26.89 on the other); left-out sum 61.43

kruonis_output.method: one bid for every gas offer of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, a combined-cycle plant's cost (gas_ccgt) plus one adder: the average of the adders each fit year gives alone on a grid of 10 EUR/MWh from 0 to 150 and of 2.5 EUR/MWh around its best, objective sum of the three zones' hourly price MAE of that year; engine of record; at Kruonis's step 60 EUR/MWh, the step of the grid whose register fits the two years best (D-115, D-164; the grid: step 0: 45, 64.56; step 15: 43.75, 62.97; step 30: 42.5, 62; step 45: 42.5, 61.51; step 60: 42.5, 61.43; step 90: 42.5, 61.59); 2023 alone 42.5 (26.89 on it, 34.54 on the other); 2024 alone 42.5 (34.54 on it, 26.89 on the other); left-out sum 61.43
